parts.latex: How many activities are on the critical path?
Determine the latest start time of activity E.
Which activity has the longest float time?

It is possible to reduce the completion time for activities C, D, G, H and K by employing more workers. The completion time for each of these activities can be reduced by a maximum of 2 weeks. What is the minimum time, in weeks, that the renovation project could take? Show working.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{2846_q6_s1}

The critical path is
$$A - B - D - F - G - I - K - L$$
$$\therefore\ 8 \text{ activities}$$

The activity with the longest float is $J$.
$$\text{Float of } J = 5 \text{ weeks}$$

Reduce $D$ by $2$ and $C$ by $1$, saving $2$ weeks.

Reduce $G$ by $2$, $H$ by $1$ and $K$ by $2$, saving $4$ weeks.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total saving} &= 6 \text{ weeks} \\ \text{Minimum time} &= 35 - 6 \\ &= 29 \text{ weeks} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds either reduction, or equivalent merit

7263.stem:
The time taken to complete each task in a building project (in weeks) is shown in the network diagram below.

\exfigure{2844_q4b_1}

figures.cap: activity network with earliest/latest start times

parts.latex: How many weeks is the whole building project expected to take?
What is the earliest start time (EST) of task H?
What series of tasks is the critical path?
What is the float time for task E?

There was a delay early in the project which resulted in task D beginning in Week 5.

Explain the impact that this delay will have on the expected completion time of the project.

solutions.latex:
The project completion time is the earliest finish time at the final node.
$$\therefore\ 16 \text{ weeks}$$

Task H starts at the node after A and D, whose earliest start time (top number) is $3$.
$$\therefore\ \text{EST of H} = 3 \text{ weeks}$$

The critical path is the path with no float, where the top and bottom numbers agree at every node ($0, 2, 4, 7, 11, 13, 16$).
$$\therefore\ A \to C \to F \to G \to J \to L$$
Check: $2 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 2 + 3 = 16$ weeks.

meta.generated_note: The arrows in the answer are task-sequence notation, not reasoning arrows.

solutions.latex:
Float time is the latest finish time of the task minus its earliest start time minus its duration.

Task E starts at the node with EST $3$ and finishes at the node with LST $10$. Its duration is $2$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{float} &= 10 - 3 - 2 \\ &= 5 \text{ weeks} \end{aligned}$$

Task D has duration $1$ week. Starting in Week 5, it finishes in Week 6, so H can start in Week 6.

H takes $2$ weeks, so it finishes in Week 8.

The latest finish time for H is Week 11, so there is still time in hand. D is not on the critical path: its float is $9 - 2 - 1 = 6$ weeks, and a delay of $5 - 2 = 3$ weeks is less than this.
$$\therefore\ \text{there is no impact: the project still takes } 16 \text{ weeks}$$
